questions.stem: According to the first paragraph, the modern university is prone to internal tension because it

options.A: pairs learning pursued for its own sake with research aimed at producing knowledge
options.B: has abandoned the study of established subjects in favor of the creation of new knowledge
options.C: serves governments that ask for economic returns and families that ask for liberal education
options.D: inherited its structure from German professors who rejected the teaching of undergraduates

questions.explanation: Correct: A) the passage describes the university as a hybrid of Newman's ideal and the German research university. Why the others are wrong: B) The passage does not say established subjects were abandoned. C) The economic demand comes from both governments and families in the second paragraph. D) The German professor was an investigator as well as a teacher, not one who rejected teaching.
questions.trap: Taking the economic pressures in paragraph two as the source of the hybrid tension in paragraph one.

questions.stem: The defenders of the economic emphasis argue that Newman's ideal

options.A: was available only to a narrow, privileged elite
options.B: ignored the value of liberal habits of judgment
options.C: could never be defended on utilitarian grounds
options.D: was introduced to justify industrial patents

questions.explanation: Correct: A) they say the leisure to pursue knowledge for its own sake was a privilege of the elite students Newman's university served. Why the others are wrong: B) Newman's view is that liberal education forms such habits, and defenders do not deny it. C) The utilitarian defense is introduced later and is not part of the defenders' reply. D) Patents are a later development in universities' economic role.
questions.trap: Confusing the defenders' historical point with the later utilitarian argument.

questions.stem: The mathematics and bacteria examples are used to support which claim?

options.A: The practical value of inquiry is often unforeseeable, so a strict focus on foreseeable returns could reduce useful results
options.B: Universities should teach only the subjects that have already been shown to produce commercial technologies
options.C: Researchers who pursue curiosities do so with the intention of producing cryptography and laboratory tools
options.D: The intrinsic dignity of the mind is a stronger argument than any appeal to practical benefit

questions.explanation: Correct: A) the passage says that if payoffs are unforeseeable, organizing around foreseeable returns would be worse at producing useful results. Why the others are wrong: B) This reverses the point of the examples. C) The passage says the results were once thought to be curiosities, not that researchers intended these uses. D) The passage says the utilitarian argument may be more persuasive to a skeptical public.
questions.trap: Reading examples of surprising usefulness as an endorsement of targeted research.

questions.stem: Which of the following, if true, would most weaken the argument from unforeseeable usefulness?

options.A: Most major practical advances in recent decades came from projects funded partly by private industry
options.B: Many mathematical results remain without any practical application after more than a century
options.C: Funding for the humanities has fallen faster than funding for engineering at most universities
options.D: Most major practical advances in recent decades came from projects aimed at a specific application from the start

questions.explanation: Correct: D) if practical advances usually come from directed work, targeting foreseeable returns would not reduce useful results. Why the others are wrong: A) Source of funding does not show whether the work was directed. B) Unused results are consistent with unpredictability. C) Funding trends do not address how useful results arise.
questions.trap: Choosing a fact about funding that has a similar theme but does not test the claim.

questions.stem: The author concludes that a university which defends itself solely by its eventual usefulness

options.A: will be more persuasive to the public than one that appeals to the dignity of the mind
options.B: will necessarily abandon research in fields that cannot promise a financial return
options.C: concedes its critics' premise that its worth lies in what it produces
options.D: has shown that Newman's ideal can be derived from a calculation of benefit

questions.explanation: Correct: C) the final paragraph says such a defense concedes that worth is measured by outputs. Why the others are wrong: A) The author grants persuasiveness earlier, but says the defense has a limit. B) The passage says such fields are pressured, but does not say they are necessarily abandoned. D) The author says the commitment cannot be derived from a calculation of benefit.
questions.trap: Taking the persuasiveness point from paragraph four as the author's conclusion.
